assessedSteps.reason: The hall loss, split groups and joint rehearsals establish a previously connected orchestra and a concrete restoration. A is the sole supported interpretation. B/C conflict with the model; D literal curtains is intentionally wrong but too easy.

All four answers are natural, constructive replies to the reopened music programme, and only C uses the reviewed target. No learner-facing example uses the title form stitch it back together with a named antecedent; C can do so without ambiguity.

A models the target in a newly reconnected reading programme. B denies the stated shared history and C denies the stated current shared hosts/timetable; both are direct contradictions rather than plausible near misses.
A new choir has no earlier whole to restore. A and C both describe reconnection of a prior group. The back/restoration boundary is supported rather than invented.

A is the only natural next turn that uses the expression and proposes joint rehearsals. B tells willing groups to remain apart and C cancels the choir; both are implausible in context. The line about three leaders wanting to sing together can more clearly say their singers want to sing together.
Exact UTF-16 span covers the target and the model explicitly names the youth theatre and earlier split; no assessed key or recording requirement is implied.

The writing prompt repeats the speaking model’s theatre/stage-closure/separate-casts/joint-rehearsals restoration pattern. Both examples and the answer-derived glossary must be regenerated for a genuinely different setting.
